title: Immutable audit signatures and CMK regional lockdown with RBAC v2 assertion
author: Aisha Patel
ci_status: pass (lint failed first run, re-run fixed auto-format issues)
description:
Motivation: customers in regulated environments require tamper-evident audit trails and strict enforcement of customer-managed key (CMK) locality. This PR introduces immutable audit signatures for every request that touches customer data and an enforcement layer that prevents use of CMKs outside of a tenant's allowed regions, with a configurable fallback to service-managed keys and a clear auditable decision path.

Summary of changes: adds a signing middleware that records an X-Redwood-Audit-Signature header (ECDSA over canonicalized audit metadata) stored alongside existing structured audit events; augments KMS policy evaluation to check key.region against tenant.allowed_regions and reject or downgrade to service-managed encryption based on tenant policy; wires attribute-driven RBAC v2 assertions so policy rules can reference kms_origin and audit_signature_verified.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-7890/cmk-region-lockdown-and-immutable-audit-signatures
- [x] Schema migration for audit_index.audit_signature (append-only)
- [x] Middleware + signer implementation (service key rotation compatible)
- [x] KMS policy evaluator changes and guardrails
- [x] RBAC v2 attribute mapping and tests
- [x] E2E regression tests and CI coverage
- [x] Ops rollout plan with feature-flagged canary across 5% of tenants

Risks and mitigations: signing increases latency on the critical path by ~0.4ms (benchmarked); signing is skipped for internal system-only calls via a new internal_identity flag. The KMS enforcement will block cross-region CMK use; default tenant policy is permissive with a warning mode to avoid unexpected failures. We added a migration that populates allowed_regions for legacy tenants using org metadata and a notification flow. For customers that rely on cross-region CMKs, operators can opt into a 'legacy-cross-region' shim that logs and downgrades instead of rejecting.

Rollout plan: feature flag rollouts: (1) audit signature middleware enabled for internal-only traffic (2) enable signing for canary tenants (5%) (3) enable enforcement in warning mode for 5% (4) enforcement on by default after 2 weeks and customer opt-in review.

Notes on compliance: signatures are persisted in audit_index and are immutable (append-only) and backed by retention/lock policies we coordinate with legal. This satisfies requirements for non-repudiation in our SOC2/RIMS controls when combined with key attestation.

Migration & operational playbook (short): new env vars: AUDIT_SIGNING_KEY_ROTATION_PERIOD, AUDIT_SIGNATURE_HEADER_NAME (defaults to X-Redwood-Audit-Signature), KMS_REGION_ENFORCE_MODE (disabled|warn|block). Ops runbook included in docs/ops/cmk-region-lockdown.md.

I intentionally kept the change modular: signing is an independent layer so other downstream consumers can opt in to verify signatures for high-sensitivity workflows.
commits_summary: 3 commits: initial signer and middleware; KMS evaluator hook + policy rules; tests and migration. Commits condensed from earlier WIP into final squashed commit on merge.
review_comments:
Marcus Chen: Security review - can we include a proof of possession check for signing keys? Suggest adding a periodic key-attestation job.
Author(Aisha Patel): Added key-attestation job and unit tests in signer_attest_test.go; attestation runs daily and emits attest.audit_key_version metric.

Lena Rodriguez: SRE - this adds a small latency; put a histogram metric and ensure fallback on signer outage.
Author: Added audit.signer.latency histogram and circuit-breaker that switches to async-signing with eventual consistency when signer health < 0.8.

Omar Farouk: Compliance - need clear exportable evidence for audits. How do we surface signatures?
Author: Added api to fetch audit signature chain for a request id (internal-only), and docs for auditors describing verification steps.

Security bot (automated): Static analysis flagged potential time-of-check/time-of-use on allowed_regions lookup; added mutex and cache invalidation in kms/evaluator.go.
Author: Addressed - added cache TTL and lock around read-modify operations.
QA: Flaky test e2e/security/cmk_region_enforce.test.ts failed on first CI run due to race in test harness; fixed by adding deterministic test fixtures. CI re-run green.
release_notes: Added immutable audit signatures (X-Redwood-Audit-Signature) and tenant CMK region enforcement. New feature flags: AUDIT_SIGNATURE_ENABLED, KMS_REGION_ENFORCE_MODE. Ops: review docs/ops/cmk-region-lockdown.md before enabling enforcement in block mode.
testing_summary: Unit tests for signer, kms evaluator, rbac mapping. Integration suite plus canary E2E validated: signer latency +0.4ms p50, no regression in throughput for standard workloads. Added smoke test to nightly regression suite.
notes_for_support: If tenants see blocked encryption calls after enabling enforcement, check tenant.allowed_regions and server logs for kms_evaluator.decision. Support can toggle KMS_REGION_ENFORCE_MODE to warn to restore functionality while investigating.
security_implications: Stronger non-repudiation guarantees; enforcement may break customers using cross-region CMKs — default mode is warn to surface issues before blocking. Signing keys are rotated and attested; private keys never leave HSM-backed KMS in production.
